lines.t: [Instrumental Intro — Dark and Mournful]
(Deep cello, distant flute, low atmospheric drones, and slow tribal drums. A lonely city beneath a darkened sky.)
The moon hangs over broken walls,
The wind moves through the empty halls.
Where songs once rose like morning fire,
The streets remember every name,
But no one answers when they call.
The stones have heard a thousand prayers,
Now silence covers them all.
A crown has fallen into dust,
A throne has lost its golden light.
Somewhere beneath the ruins,
A voice begins to cry.
Somewhere beneath the ruins,
A voice begins to cry.
Not for the treasures buried,
But for the love left behind.
Oh, Jerusalem, lift your eyes,
Though sorrow covers all your skies.
The night is deep, the road is long,
The broken heart still has a song.
You wandered far, you lost your way,
You traded truth for empty praise.
But through the tears and through the pain,
Will you seek The Lord again?
The mothers count the empty chairs,
The fathers whisper desperate prayers.
The children dream of distant doors,
Of fields they knew in days before.
The harvest vanished from the land,
The hungry reach with trembling hands.
The watchmen stand upon the towers,
Their shadows stretch across the stones.
They see the roads that lead to nowhere,
Do you hear the people groan?
The city wears her grief like ashes,
Her beauty fades beneath the rain.
Will He clean her stain?
Oh, Jerusalem, lift your eyes,
Though sorrow covers all your skies.
The night is deep, the road is long,
The broken heart still has a song.
You wandered far, you lost your way,
You traded truth for empty praise.
But through the tears and through the pain,
Will you seek The Lord again?
[Instrumental Interlude — Haunting]
(The drums grow heavier. Low strings swell. A distant male choir echoes beneath the melody.)
The gates are cold beneath the heavens,
The lamps have faded one by one.
The voices that proclaimed their greatness
Have vanished with the setting sun.
She looks upon the distant mountains,
Where once her celebrations rang.
The memory of ancient gladness
The memory of ancient gladness
Cuts deeper than a blade.
What have we done with all Your kindness?
Where did we hide Your living word?
Why did we chase the fleeting shadows
And turn our backs to The Lord?
